business_problem: Pitney Bowes needed a managed multi-cloud database that could scale its ecommerce logistics business, keep freight data available in real time, and eliminate downtime and heavy administration across a large shipping network.
solution_summary: Pitney Bowes standardized ecommerce logistics workloads on MongoDB Atlas running on AWS so freight and parcel data could stay close to application processing while operations remained simple. Atlas is provisioned inside the private side of the company's VPC, which reduces networking complexity while preserving security and compliance expectations. The platform handles production backup, disaster recovery, and version upgrades with minimal human effort, so teams can move cluster-wide to a new release in minutes without taking the system offline. MongoDB now acts as the backbone of Pitney Bowes' ecommerce logistics business and also supports other use cases such as manifesting data stores and data retrieval for physical processing centers. That data platform gives the company a centralized view of freight across facilities, reduces total cost of ownership, and leaves more engineering capacity for higher-value supply-chain and edge-computing work instead of day-to-day database care.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores and serves freight and ecommerce logistics data while providing managed backup, recovery, and upgrades for Pitney Bowes.

data_flow: Freight, parcel, and manifesting data are written into MongoDB Atlas inside Pitney Bowes' private VPC-connected cloud environment, logistics applications query that shared data in real time across facilities, and the platform supports downstream shipping and processing workflows.
business_outcome: MongoDB Atlas gave Pitney Bowes a scalable logistics backbone with no-downtime upgrades, lower operational cost, and a shared freight view that supports its $1 billion-plus ecommerce business.
